newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cellular industry 1996 growth slowed - study.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cellular industry 1996 growth slowed - study.

text.p: Growth in net new subscribers in the U.S. cellular market slowed to nine million in 1996 from almost 10 million in 1995, according to a study by The Strategis Group.
Strategis, formerly known as MTA-EMCI, said handset market share in 1996 was 40 percent for Motorola Inc, 20 percent for Nokia, and 10 percent each for AB L M Ericsson and NEC Corp.
About 20 manufacturers share the remaining 20 percent share, the study said.

"The challenge ahead for the cellular industry is to recognize it is in the first phase of a maturing industry with increasing competition on the horizon," said Elliott Hamilton, a Strategis vice president.
The study forecasts that over 19 million new cellular subscribers will be added over the next five years -- bringing the total number of subscribers to over 62 million in 2001.

The study predicts that by 2001 there will be an additional 26 million Personal Communication Service subscribers, which will give wireless phones an overall market penetration of nearly 47 percent of U.S. households. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
